articles.title: Polls have now closed in 8 states as midterm results begin rolling in
articles.summary: Election night is here, with the first polls beginning to close as voters across the United States cast their ballots in the 2026 midterms . And with control of Congress up for grabs, the stakes are high for both parties as President Trump heads into his final two years in office. Democrats are seeking to regain control of both the House and Senate, while Republicans, who have held narrow majorities in both chambers since January 2025, are seeking to retain control. In the House, there are 435 seats. And while all of them are technically up for grabs, roughly 80% (or about 350 seats) are not considered competitive. The GOP currently holds 218 seats, compared with 214 held by Democrats. To retake control of the House , Democrats would need a net gain of three seats. In the Senate, there are 100 seats, with 35 up for grabs and 12 or so considered competitive . Republicans currently hold 53 seats compared with 45 held by Democrats. There are two independents — Sens. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Angus King of Maine — who caucus with the Democrats. To wrest back control of the Senate, Democrats would need a net gain of four seats. To maintain Senate control, Republicans could still lose a net of three seats, since a 50-50 split would give Vice President JD Vance the tiebreaking vote. There are also 36 gubernatorial races and numerous ballot measures to keep an eye on. Trump, whose approval ratings are at or near all-time lows, spent the last month campaigning in battleground states, urging voters to "pretend" he's on the ballot to encourage higher turnout in hopes that it'll help Republicans avert a so-called blue wave . Some members of the GOP, however, appear to be bracing for one. "It could be quite a brutal evening," one senior GOP official told Politico . "Once the dominoes start falling, it becomes hard to stop them." articles.title: Tennessee murderer captured in Missouri after prison escape and truck theft
articles.summary: Authorities have captured a convicted murderer who evaded law enforcement for more than a week after escaping from a Tennessee prison. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation announced Tuesday that Jacob Morley was back in custody. He was arrested near Kansas City, Missouri, investigators said. "Thank you to the public for your assistance, vigilance, and the tips provided during this investigation," the bureau said in a statement. "We also thank all of our law enforcement partners for their continued efforts to safely bring this search to a successful conclusion." Investigators got a tip Tuesday morning that Morley had been hiding in a shed at a hunting camp around Marion, Illinois, some 320 miles south of Chicago, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said in a statement. Authorities also learned a truck had been stolen from the property. Missouri State Highway Patrol said it handled Morley's arrest alongside multiple partner agencies, after Tennessee authorities reported that Morley may be traveling through Missouri, based on footage obtained through Flock cameras. The arrest happened around 11:30 a.m. local time near Norborne, a small city about an hour's drive from Kansas City, the state agency said. Authorities said they also recovered three firearms that had previously been reported stolen inside the truck. Little information about the inmate's escape and the multi-state search for him has been made available since Morley broke out of prison. But investigators said more will be released as it becomes available. Morley, 28, was serving a life sentence at the Northwest Correctional Complex in an isolated part of Tiptonville, a town roughly 90 miles from Memphis in northwestern Tennessee. He had been convicted of killing a coworker four years ago, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. Correctional officers discovered Morley was missing from the prison at around 11:30 p.m. local time on Oct. 25, the department said. While parsing security cameras later on, investigators said they saw footage of Morley escaping the complex while wearing his prison uniform by slipping through a fence on the property. Authorities released additional security footage two days later that showed the inmate stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350, with Tennessee plates and a logo for Lindamood Planting Company on the side door, in the early hours of Oct. 27. It was stolen from Lake County, which includes Tiptonville, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said. The truck was located later the same day in Marion, Illinois, which is about 150 miles north of Tiptonville, the investigative bureau said . Morley's whereabouts were unknown at the time. The bureau had said earlier in the week that Morley was on its "most wanted" list, as various agencies, including the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, the governor's office and U.S. Marshals, offered combined rewards of up to $17,500 for information leading to his arrest. Investigators haven't shared details about how exactly the inmate escaped, beyond the fact that he breached a fence at the prison. Morley received a lifetime prison sentence for murdering Cody Birchfield, his former coworker, in 2022. Authorities said Birchfield's body was found in a box under Morley's home in Tennessee's Carter County after he had been missing for several weeks. In addition to first-degree murder, Morley was convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism and evading arrest, as he fled when deputies arrived at his home in 2022. Authorities said the manhunt for him at the time ended in North Carolina. Northwest Correctional Complex is a men's prison with the capacity to hold 1,776 inmates under varying degrees of security, from the lowest level up to maximum, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. It also houses minors who have been convicted of crimes as adults. Multiple violent incidents have taken place inside the prison in recent years, some of which involved attacks between inmates and prison staff. In July, a grand jury returned dozens of indictments over the murders of five inmates, assaults against staff and other acts of violence. At a recent meeting of the Tennessee Inmate Disciplinary Oversight Board, members discussed ongoing problems in the prison and suggested issues with leadership played a role. articles.title: DOJ ramps up Alaska Senate race probe with target letters and new subpoenas: Sources
articles.summary: The Justice Department in recent days has continued moving at an aggressive clip in ramping up its criminal investigation into the Alaska U.S. Senate race, sources familiar with the matter tell ABC News, with prosecutors in the process of issuing more than 100 subpoenas and at least twenty target letters and preservation notices alerting individuals they are targets of the probe. The investigation began accelerating last week after The New York Times detailed alleged efforts by Democrats and some in Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign to recruit Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, to be on the ballot with incumbent Republican Dan S. Sullivan. The target letters, which are being issued to Democrats whom investigators believe were involved in the recruitment effort , are an unusual step in such an early juncture in the investigation. Peltola denies knowledge of 'any other candidate' on Alaska Senate ballot besides herself and incumbent Dan Sullivan Among the recipients are Marc Elias, sources said, an attorney frequently attacked by Republicans over his extensive involvement in election-related litigation on behalf of Democrats. "No one should be surprised that President Trump's Department of Justice is targeting me and my law firm on Election Day," Elias said in a statement. "This administration has repeatedly weaponized the DOJ against the President's political enemies despite zero evidence of wrongdoing, and we are the latest targets. We will not be intimidated by a sham investigation." A target letter, which is typically used by the Justice Department to alert an individual they are a "target" of a federal grand jury investigation, does not mean an individual will ultimately face federal charges. According to sources, the letters indicate that a grand jury empaneled in Alaska is probing possible conspiracy and donor fraud related offenses. Appearing on Fox News Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said that further DOJ action could be triggered in the event Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses, saying, "There is a scenario where the incumbent Sen. Sullivan could lose but really he didn't lose -- really because of ranked-based, it's clear that voters were confused." Charly Triballeau/AFP via Getty Images - PHOTO: Sen. Dan Sullivan gives a thumbs up to passing vehicles as he campaigns along a roadside on Election Day during the midterm elections in, Anchorage, Alaska, November 3, 2026. "Again, that's why you need to preserve the ballots because you need to look at the individual ballots potentially to see if there was voter confusion, if it's obvious from the ballot itself that the voter, or likely that the voter intended to vote for Sen. Sullivan but was confused because of the fraud that's taken place there," Blanche said. U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason, who dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the race if Sen. Sullivan loses, said in her ruling that once ballots were cast, an investigation into voter intent would be "impossible" because the government would have to preserve voter secrecy even if ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were somehow segregated. A DOJ spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment from ABC News. articles.title: Minnesota voters leave 'I Voted' stickers at memorial sites for Alex Pretti and Renee Good
articles.summary: Alex Pretti was shot by ICE agents on 24 January 2026 during a large-scale federal immigration enforcement operation. Photograph: Tim Evans/AFP/Getty Images Minnesota voters left “I Voted” stickers on memorial sites for Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good, the two US citizens killed by federal immigration officials earlier this year. Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care unit nurse at the Veterans Affairs medical center in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and Good, a writer and mother of three, were killed during a large-scale immigration enforcement operation in the Minneapolis region in January. Donald Trump’s aggressive and violent mass deportation campaign has been a key issue for voters across the country during this midterm cycle, and has played a large part in Minnesota’s election. “I knew Alex Pretti,” said a retired physician who worked with Pretti and asked only to use his first name, Arne. “I just knew that he was a competent nurse – a really, really liked guy. And he was assassinated.” Arne left his “I Voted” sticker at the memorial site and choked up when speaking about his vote, Pretti and when federal immigration officials killed him. Related: ICE rapidly re-arresting immigrants released after winning court petitions Another voter, Mike F, who withheld his last name for privacy reasons, left his sticker at Good’s memorial site: “I felt like my vote felt a little bit more in touch with some of the things that happened earlier this year in the city,” he said. “So I felt like it was just the right thing to do – to come pay some respects and attach my vote to what happened here.” At the end of 2025 and early this year, Minnesota became a central target for the Trump administration. Federal immigration officials descended on the area during “Operation Metro Surge”. Community groups organized rapid response teams throughout the city to prevent officials from arresting immigrants, and the situation escalated after Good and Pretti were killed. Many groups involved in the immigration rapid response work have since shifted their attention on to the elections. In Minnesota, voters are choosing a Senator and governor, as well as House candidates. “The country has humiliated itself by putting in a bad man, a very, very bad character,” Arne said of the president. “Today is a chance for America to say whether they support this kind of thing.” If they don’t oppose it, “then fuck America”, he added. In a primarily Somali neighborhood elsewhere in Minneapolis, the Rev Shandon Klein, a progressive pastor from the Park Avenue United Methodist church, said she was “keeping a watchful eye over the polling place just to make sure I’m a non-anxious presence that’s available here and just ensuring that everybody has access to voting. “There’s a general, just, feeling of empowerment and really excited to get out there and vote,” Klein said. So far, no federal law enforcement officials have been spotted, despite threats by the Trump administration to deploy them to voting sites. articles.title: Tail component broke off before deadly Florida jet crash, investigators say
articles.summary: Investigators continue to work to “gather critical evidence” of what caused a Bahamas-bound Learjet to crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Nov. 1. At a Nov. 3 National Transportation Safety Board press conference, spokesperson Tom Chapman called the investigation a "big puzzle to try to put together,” with work at the impact site hampered by severe storms. The NTSB will be working with local public works teams this week to remove water from the crater caused by the plane’s impact, where investigators expect to find airplane components that will help determine what went wrong. Chapman had one notable development to share: The aircraft's left elevator — a control surface on the tail that controls the up-and-down pitch of the plane — was found in three pieces between about 1.3 and 3.8 miles from the crash site. Investigators believe it separated from the plane before impact. Chapman urged members of the public who find wreckage not to touch it and to call authorities. Weather remains a key focus of the investigation, Chapman said. He also appeared to rule out a connection between the crash and the plane's proximity to President Trump's Mar-a-Lago Club. Earlier in the day, Jeff Gregory, 55, of Gilbertsville, Penn., was identified as the plane's pilot. The crash killed all nine people aboard,  including his copilot, Nathalia Filgueiras , and seven passengers, Fox 29 reports . The families of Filgueiras and the passengers had previously confirmed their deaths. Camila Corteleti identified her 20-year-old daughter as one of the pilots of the private jet, the New York Times reported. A joint statement from the families was released on social media. "With broken hearts, our families share that Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, their children Emma and Charlie, Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina were among those lost aboard the flight that went down near Greenacres, Florida, on November 1," the statement said. A tribute to Sharp and her family was posted on her Instagram page , saying, "On behalf of friends and family, it is with a heavy heart that we share that our dearest Helen was taken from us too soon. If you knew Helen, you knew how full of life she was. She simply radiated." In a news conference on Nov. 2, investigators said weather conditions were a major factor in the federal investigation into the fatal crash. The NTSB told reporters on Nov. 2 that ice was forming on the jet as it experienced moderate turbulence. Miami air traffic control granted the pilot permission to climb from 35,000 feet to 37,000 feet to avoid precipitation, but shortly afterward, an emergency was declared with a mayday call. Air traffic control audio posted on LiveATC captured the crew's comments leading up to the crash. Someone in the cockpit can be heard saying "Mayday, mayday," reporting the plane was descending at 10,000 feet per minute, Reuters reported. "We're going to crash into the ground," the person, since identified as Filgueiras, said. The Learjet 60, which had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas, went down at about 12:50 p.m. ET near Cresthaven, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. A man who was leaving the area of the crash sustained a leg injury, officials said. Dashcam footage posted to social media by an eyewitness showed the aircraft falling toward the ground beside a road and exploding into a fireball, narrowly missing cars and homes. The impact left a "massive crater" near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at a news conference. About 600 residents were evacuated to two shelters, he said. People stand near a crater formed after the Learjet 60 crashed. Vanessa Lara/via REUTERS "We have a lot of work to do on scene — this will be a several-day process," NTSB senior investigator Timothy Monville said during Nov. 2's news conference. "The biggest obstacle we're going to have is recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway." The NTSB said it will interview witnesses to the accident as part of its investigation and encouraged anyone with relevant information, videos or audio to contact the NTSB by email at witness@ntsb.gov. Chapman also told reporters that, according to records, a cockpit voice recorder was installed, but the NTSB doesn't know whether it was still on board. "Sometimes these things change over time," Chapman said. "Of course we're very hopeful that we can recover it. Too early to know, but that will be very important data." What we know about the victims Among the victims was the private jet's pilot, Gregory, a husband and father from Gilbertsville, Pa., outside Philadelphia. Federal Aviation Administration records obtained by the Associated Press say he held airline transport pilot and flight instructor certificates. Friends described Gregory as a devout Christian. They believe his was the voice heard reciting a prayer in the background of Filgueiras's final radio transmissions to air traffic control as the plane descended, the AP reports. Thomas Noetzel, director of operations at Upper Jets, the company that operated the flight, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregory's wife and children. "Jeff was also a personal friend, and knowing him has made me a better person," Noetzel wrote. Gregory's former employer, East Coast Jets, a private jet company in Allentown, said he was an aviator with years of experience , according to the New York Times. He worked there in 2016 and 2017. "We are deeply saddened to learn that Captain Jeff Gregory was among those who lost their lives in yesterday's tragic aviation accident in Palm Beach," a spokesperson for East Coast Jets said in a statement on Nov. 2. His copilot Filgueiras's mother said she earned her pilot's license at age 17. The 20-year-old had logged more than 1,300 hours of flight time and was working for a private charter firm based in Fort Lauderdale, according to her mother. Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras itsnatfilg/Threads NFL running back Joe Mixon was among those paying tribute to Gregory and Filgueiras . In an X post on Nov. 3, the former Pro Bowler said he had recently flown with the pilots on the very same aircraft. "They were incredible professionals and genuinely wonderful people," Mixon, who most recently played for the Houston Texans, wrote. He added, "My heart, thoughts, and prayers go out to the grieving families and loved ones of everyone on board. A tragic reminder of how fragile life is. Love on your loved ones while you can, because you never know what tomorrow may bring." Absolutely devastated by yesterday’s tragic plane crash in Florida and the loss of all nine lives. I flew on that exact aircraft last month with those same two pilots. They were incredible professionals and genuinely wonderful people. Hearing the young woman’s story and learning… — ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) November 2, 2026 According to the Palm Beach Post , the crash also killed Helen Sharp, 40, her husband, Adam Robinson, 45, and their two young children. Sharp's father, 70-year-old Dudley Sharp, confirmed the deaths to the outlet. "It's quite a blow," he told the Palm Beach Post. "We had a daughter, her husband and two grandchildren on the plane." Family members of the seven passengers killed in the Nov. 1 crash released a joint statement on Facebook that also identifies the other three passengers: Anita Maria Cetina, Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr. "With broken hearts, our families share that Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, their children Emma and Charlie, Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and Anita Maria Cetina were among those lost aboard the flight that went down near Greenacres, Florida, on November 1," the statement said. "Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were the light of their lives.  Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever.  Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives.  Their loss will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return." "Charmi and Rachel were full of joy and adventure," the statement continued. "They loved their people fiercely, fully and without hesitation. From the moment they met, they were all in on each other and the life they were building. They are deeply loved, and we will miss them endlessly. Anita Maria cared for Emma and Charlie with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family.  She showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion." Reed and Fehr were hailed as “two extraordinary individuals” in a post from the Arca Boutique Hotel in Honduras, which they co-owned. View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram The families also thanked first responders, investigators and the Palm Beach community for "their care," as well as "everyone who reached out with love." They added: "Our hearts are also with the families of the pilots, who are grieving alongside us." Robinson was a tech entrepreneur from Austin, according to his LinkedIn page. He described himself as the founder and CEO for RB2B and Retention.com. He also once hosted the podcast Ten Years in the Making , in which he shared conversations with e-commerce founders. In one 2023 episode with former aviation entrepreneur Lolita Petrossov, Robinson spoke about how flying private "became part of my identity." A fellow tech entrepreneur, Jesse Ouellette, shared a tribute on LinkedIn, saying Robinson had helped him when he was building his company. "He became a friend and someone I saw eye to eye with on how to build software companies," said Ouellette. "He could disagree with you about almost anything, and somehow you'd walk away liking him even more." Robinson last posted on LinkedIn on the day of his death, promoting a debate he and Ouellette had scheduled for Nov. 3. Sharp was a sculptural ceramic artist, according to her Instagram account . A tribute posted on her page said she founded a PR company, Influential PR. The pair, according to the same post, met while Sharp was living abroad in Buenos Aires, Argentina. What we know The aircraft crashed in a residential area in Greenacres. Anadolu via Getty Images The Learjet 60 took off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. FAA records list the owner as a Delaware corporation. The National Weather Service had a flood watch in effect for the crash area, Palm Beach County, through Nov. 2, with rain expected on and off across South Florida. In air traffic control audio posted on LiveATC, someone in the cockpit said they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides." The Associated Press reported the crew also asked to climb. Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting the plane was suddenly descending at 10,000 feet per minute. Seconds later, the person declared an emergency, with the descent rate reaching 20,000 feet per minute. Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground," before reporting the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane began to bank. Flightradar24 data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute. The last words heard from the cockpit were "we're out of time." Driver Aki Kuusisto's dashcam footage captured the moment the jet hit the ground. "I heard a whistling noise, a big bang, and I saw a fireball," he told CBS News . "It felt like it was right next to us... you could feel it in the car." The jet is reported to have descended at a peak of 32,000 feet per minute. Anadolu via Getty Images Accuweather reported that thunderstorms in the area produced heavy rainfall and lightning.  AP reports that the pilots were warned by controllers about the looming storms as they crossed into Florida and the FAA published an official warning about the weather prior to the plane's departure on Nov. 1. According to AccuWeather, the tops of some of the storm clouds reached up to 45,000 feet, making it difficult for planes to fly over. The plane may not have been able to detect the updrafts that can intensify precipitation, as AccuWeather's Dan DePodwin said that the weather radars on planes have limitations. Chapman said that the investigators are yet to determine what the weather conditions were at 35,000 feet, the altitude the plane was flying at when problems were first reported by the copilot.  He added that the investigators hope to recover the cockpit voice recorder. 'A cataclysmic plane crash' Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis told reporters during a Nov. 1 briefing that there was "a lot of debris" that was strewn over a "pretty significant distance." "It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis said. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road." Transportation Secretary Duffy called the crash a "horrific tragedy" and said the FAA and Department of Transportation would be investigating the incident. Anthony Blackmon, who lives around 500 feet from the site of the crash, told NBC Miami that debris from the crash struck his home. "Debris was everywhere," he said. "Debris hit my house. Everything was on fire. The road was on fire. I've always seen it on the news, never thought it would happen so close to somebody like how it happened today." Adam Itayem told WPTV , "It sounded like a loud boom. I thought it was thunder," adding, "I saw a big crater in the ground and water coming out of the crater and a big fire too." "I heard and felt the boom," Andrew Mannino told CNN , saying he saw a "large black cloud immerse in the air," adding, "The power immediately went out and is still out." Around 600 people were evacuated by Palm Beach County authorities while federal officials investigate the crash. "We're waiting for someone to give us answers about what we're going to do, because they're not even letting us into the community to get our clothes," local resident Jesus Solorzano told WPTV. articles.title: 2 people dead, hundreds rescued amid severe flooding in Florida
articles.summary: Two people were killed -- one of whom died in a vehicle -- and hundreds of others were rescued since Sunday as a storm brought severe flooding in Palm Bay, Florida, according to Palm Bay Mayor Rob Medina. The deceased victims have been identified by Florida officials as Joshua Bennett, 34, and Archie Richards, 78 Emergency crews rescued hundreds of people from flooded areas using boats and special high-water vehicles, Medina said in a press conference Tuesday. Port St. Lucie Police Department - PHOTO: In this screen grab from a video posted to social media, a truck travels through flood waters in Port St. Lucie, Fla., on Nov. 3, 2026. Greg Lovett/USA Today Network via Reuters - PHOTO: Workers from A1 Moving move a voting machine out of Magnolia Park Town Hall polling precinct after flooding in the parking lot forced them to move to another location during the US midterm election in Magnolia Park, Fla., on Nov. 3, 2026. Some homes suffered major damage. One family reported that 38 inches of water had filled their living room, Medina told reporters. "That is devastation within our city," Medina said. Officials warned that flooding could continue even after the rain stops because water may take several days to drain. They urged residents to stay away from flooded roads, fast-moving water and downed power lines. Election 2026 live updates: Americans cast their votes Florida Fish & Wildlife - PHOTO: FWC officers have deployed to St. Lucie County to conduct rescue operations and assist residents affected by this week’s historic rainfall and flooding. Flooding has also affected other parts of Florida, including St. Lucie, Martin and Palm Beach counties. State officials said they are working with local leaders to determine how much damage the storm caused. A low-pressure system over the Gulf led to continuous onshore flow over the Florida peninsula on Sunday and Monday. articles.title: Trump says U.S. will halt $4 billion in annual aid to Israel and shift to selling arms
articles.summary: President Donald Trump declared Tuesday that the U.S. will end nearly $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel, an unusually timed announcement on Election Day that could set up a standoff with Congress. The president said on "Fox and Friends" that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed "months ago" to stop the aid by the end of the year. "They're fine with it because they've become a very successful country," Trump said. "They don't need it. And we won't be paying anymore...we won't be paying Israel. We'll help Israel if they need it. They've been a great ally." The announcement could portend a significant shift in the U.S.-Israel relationship, which has long been underpinned by billions of dollars in American military assistance. Under a 10-year agreement signed during the Obama administration, the U.S. committed to providing Israel with $38 billion in military aid between 2019 and 2028. The earlier time frame raises questions about how the administration intends to suddenly halt the assistance, and whether Congress would need to approve the change. More than 90 percent of the money is directed to American defense companies, essentially never leaving the U.S. The Pentagon referred questions to the White House, which did not respond to a request for comment. The Israeli embassy could not be reached for comment. Trump, in the interview on Tuesday morning, said the annual assistance to Israel is a "bad talking point" for Democrats, including Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. "The left uses the $4 billion payment … as a signal of unfairness. And we can't allow that to happen. I don't like that. … It's almost too easy to target." Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.), who unsuccessfully pushed to cut military assistance to Israel while in Congress, suggested the announcement was motivated by Republicans' political troubles ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. "Amazing how being on the verge of Republicans getting wiped out in the midterms changes hearts and minds," Greene wrote on social media. "Trump getting permission from Netanyahu to end annual aid to Israel isn't going to change today's election results. But it does show you how bad the polling is on that issue." The announcement also comes just a week after Israel's parliamentary elections left Netanyahu fighting to hold onto power. His Likud party emerged with the most seats, but his right-wing coalition fell short of the 61 seats needed for a majority, teeing up difficult negotiations to form a new government. Israel's standing in the United States has eroded over the past three years amid public outrage over the country's actions in the Gaza war. Many Democrats increasingly favor conditioning if not outright ending U.S military aid to Israel. A growing number of Republicans, eager to reduce U.S. military interventions abroad, see Israel as an obstacle to that goal. Israel is categorized as a major non-NATO ally, a designation which prioritizes it for arms sales and transfers of excess American military equipment. The vast majority of the military funding comes in the form of financing that allows Israel to buy U.S. military equipment. It traditionally includes $3.3 billion in foreign military financing and another $500 million for cooperative missile defense programs. The funding counts for less than one percent of the annual U.S. federal budget. Netanyahu has hinted for years that Israel will have to become more independent of U.S. military financing. He told CBS News earlier this year that he wanted to reduce U.S. support to zero. Trump insisted the Israeli leader first broached the topic. Netanyahu said, '"It would be appropriate if we don't receive aid,' because he understands that this is one of their points of contention." But Netanyahu is also keen to maintain U.S.-Israeli defense cooperation, especially on technology. Some in Israeli and American circles want to push for more such partnerships. articles.title: An unlikely player in the Michigan Senate race: Haley Stevens's fiancé
articles.summary: Months before the high-stakes Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, Jason Turkish took such a hands-on role in Rep. Haley Stevens's campaign that her senior staff called a meeting without her to devise how to restrict his role, according to multiple people familiar with the meeting. Turkish was seen as relatively new to Stevens's orbit. Most of the congresswoman's senior staff knew him as a top donor some had met earlier in the campaign, which launched in 2025. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. By early June, Stevens and Turkish were said to be secretly engaged, according to multiple former campaign staffers who said the one-time donor had become Stevens's most important adviser. Stevens soon added him to private campaign text chains, one of the reasons staff called a meeting to figure out how to curtail his interactions with the team, according to one of the people familiar with the meeting. Tensions between staffers and a candidate's spouse or significant other are not uncommon in a campaign's intense atmosphere. They tend to erupt in crisis moments, and Stevens was facing tough polling in her race with Abdul El-Sayed. Now questions about Turkish's role in Stevens's primary campaign have been revived in the general election's closing hours, after the Democratic congresswoman's 11th-hour reversal of support for El-Sayed, the progressive Democrat who won the primary. This account is based on interviews with more than a dozen former Stevens campaign aides and other people familiar with the campaign. Stevens, 43, said that "any campaign staff being directly quoted in this article, I was made miserable by working with them." Asked whether she felt her campaign staff was trying to push out Turkish or limit his influence in any way, Stevens said, "I have nothing else to say about the campaign at this time." Turkish, a 39-year-old disability lawyer and political fundraiser, would not comment on whether staff sought to curtail his role, but he provided to The Washington Post emails from June and July showing that staff continued to reach out and consult him on campaign matters. He declined to address specific claims by former campaign staff on the record. "I was Haley Stevens's energetic and passionate supporter from the very launch of this campaign," he said. "And while the campaign ended in defeat, it also ended in our marriage. And along the path of that campaign, we spent thousands of hours together and around a campaign. And there were good days and bad days, but we lived it together, and we wouldn't trade it for anything." Turkish lives in Huntington Woods, a suburb north of Detroit, and works in Southfield as a managing partner at Nyman Turkish, a litigation and disability law firm. The Detroit News reported that the two met after Stevens's 2022 reelection campaign through David Kramer, a mutual friend. Stevens initially backed El-Sayed after their bruising primary, even telling people he was a "great candidate," but over the course of the general election, her public support for the candidate grew more strained, particularly as it related to El-Sayed's stance on Israel's war with Hamas, where he has become a leading voice denouncing U.S. support in what he labels a "genocide." Turkish endorsed El-Sayed's opponent in the key Senate race, Republican Mike Rogers, days before Stevens shocked the political world by backing Rogers and appearing with him at church on Sunday with Turkish. In an interview revealing his choice, he told the Detroit News that he saw an "escalation" in the Democratic nominee's rhetoric around Israel. Stevens's endorsement has led some close to her to express concern about Turkish's influence on her decision, including longtime friends, one who spoke with her as recently as Saturday night, mere hours before she backed Rogers on Sunday. The endorsement has effectively led Stevens to be excommunicated from her state's party, with the head of the Michigan Democratic Party writing that she was "not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future." Stevens said "any suppositions that Jason Turkish influenced me on Israel or campaign positions is absurd." Late Monday night, Stevens posted a lengthy explanation for her decision on X that lamented how "some critics have also dragged my fiancé into this, suggesting he or others must have made my decision for me." "Think about what that says. A woman can serve in Congress, run statewide, and fight for her convictions, and still be told that when she makes a choice people dislike, someone else must be pulling the strings," she wrote. "That is sexism dressed up as political analysis." One friend who spoke with Stevens said the congresswoman reassured her Saturday night that she would "never" rescind her endorsement of El-Sayed. "That primary was particularly brutal. For all involved," the friend said. "I feel that there is like an allegiance to him because he was there for her during a particularly dark and stressful time." But one aide said Stevens trusted Turkish and often valued his insight, particularly on Israel, because she agreed with him more than with her advisers, who were pushing her to be less supportive of Israel. After her endorsement of Rogers, many Israel supporters have applauded both Stevens and Turkish for what they view as a tough, gutsy stance. "By the time I got to the place where I was ready to do it, I would have been living a lie to a lot of people and in community. ... There was no way to circle the square," Stevens told the Detroit News on Monday. Stevens's senior staff first grew troubled by Turkish's campaign influence around June, people familiar with the campaign said. According to multiple people familiar with the exchanges, Turkish started berating staff for their work, particularly perplexed that he, a Stevens supporter, was being served digital ads about the campaign. He wanted more spent on digital fundraising, and he summoned a senior digital campaign staffer to his law office and yelled at her over the kind of digital content and fundraising emails the campaign was creating, the people said. He told a press aide that she was "not serving Haley well," two people familiar with the conversation recalled. Turkish would also send the congresswoman a list of hurtful tweets people were writing about her, four people familiar with Turkish's influence on Stevens said. Campaign staff also worried that when Turkish was the last person to speak with Stevens before an interview or event, she would stray from the campaign's talking points, the people said. "He was not a calming presence, in a way that in hindsight should have been more alarming," said Caitlin Legacki, a former top adviser to Stevens's campaign. "It was very strange. I have never seen anything like it." One former Stevens aide said campaign staff worked to prevent Turkish from showing up to events because of how he undermined staff. If he arrived, the person said, they would redirect cameras or reposition Stevens so that he could not draw the attention of the press. Before events, they said he often suggested rewriting talking points and insisted on joining Stevens's briefings before media appearances. The team tried to control his influence with two guardrails, multiple people said: Making sure he was not the last person to speak with Stevens before a public-facing event, and outlining how he was only allowed to go directly through the campaign's manager, Sam Barrett, not directly to lower-level staff, according to multiple sources familiar with the guardrails. "It did not work in the sense that he had any less influence on Haley," said Legacki, who left the campaign after it became public she was also working for the tech company Palantir while advising the campaign. Stevens said in an interview for this article that Legacki "was fired" because "of undisclosed conflicts." The changes meant Stevens's schedule was sometimes altered to ensure she spoke with a campaign staffer, and no one else, before certain events or calls, the people said. "We would organize the schedule to make sure there was a staff member who would be the last person talking to her because she did an interview or a donor call," said a person familiar with the campaign. Longtime friends say the couple grew even closer after her defeat. The morning after Stevens's primary loss to El-Sayed - a closer result than the polls anticipated - former Michigan governor James Blanchard (D) called her, thinking she would need some consoling, he said. Instead, she sounded ebullient. "I'm getting married!" she told Blanchard. articles.title: “历史最大黑客洗劫案”！一切始于一场“假面试”
articles.summary: 加密货币交易所币安（Binance）遭遇史上规模最大的数字资产盗窃案， 63亿美元在一次精心策划的多阶段攻击中被窃取 。而事件的起点，则是一场专门针对该公司工程师的虚假招聘面试。 据英国《金融时报》和彭博社报道，币安周二（11月3日）发布迄今最详细的调查报告，将此次攻击归因于黑客组织TraderTraitor，并披露攻击者综合运用社会工程学手段、恶意软件及人工智能工具，历时数月完成渗透。币安联席首席执行官Richard Teng表示， “这不是一次单一错误或单一漏洞，而是一场历经数月精心构建的攻击行动。” 此次事件已超越今年早些时候Bybit交易所的15亿美元盗窃案，成为数字资产史上最大规模的黑客攻击。尽管案情震惊市场，但市场反应相对克制——比特币在事件曝光后一度下跌逾4%至约76000美元，截至周二已回升至约77600美元。币安表示将自行承担财务损失，并称已基本补足被盗加密资产。 假面试为引，三名工程师相继沦陷 报道称，根据币安调查报告，此次攻击的核心突破口是一场精心设计的虚假招聘流程，历时数月、分阶段完成对币安内部系统的渗透。 今年6月，币安第一名工程师在下载一款被篡改的软件程序时，无意间将自身角色及部分钱包基础设施团队同事的身份暴露给了攻击者。 币安表示，该异常行为虽被系统检测到，涉事设备也随即被更换，但在此之前，相关信息已遭泄露。 同年9月，第二名工程师通过一个求职平台被一名自称某公司项目总监的人联系，随后参与了一场“工作面试”。币安报告显示，对方在面试过程中主动分享个人社交媒体主页，“包括在平台上发布的个人照片和视频，以建立信任感”，币安将此描述为“比以往所见更为高级和欺骗性的社会工程学手段”。 在随后通过社交聊天应用进行的第二轮面试中，另一名自称该虚假公司首席执行官的人要求该工程师下载一份面试作业文件。 这份文件内嵌恶意代码，下载行为未被检测系统拦截，由此成为整个攻击链条中最关键的突破口。 币安报告对该恶意软件的技术手段作出描述： “该恶意软件采用了复杂的混淆与规避技术，包括将合法开发工具组件替换为恶意版本，以执行命令并与攻击者控制的外部服务器建立通信。” 内部AI工具成帮凶，攻击者层层扩大控制范围 据报道，获得第二名工程师的被攻陷笔记本电脑后，攻击者并未就此止步，而是借助币安自身的内部AI工具，进一步横向渗透至其他工程师的设备。 根据报告，攻击者利用该受感染设备及币安内部AI工具，先后控制了第一名工程师和第三名工程师的笔记本电脑。 第一名工程师拥有代码发布权限，这一权限随即被黑客加以利用。 币安报告指出，攻击者通过内部AI工具获取了对部分系统的控制权，但报告未具体说明该工具的名称及被利用的具体方式。 在正式攻击发生前九天，攻击者已悄然渗透至两名与数字钱包业务相关工程师的电脑。 10月29日，即黑客事件当日，攻击者登录第三名工程师的笔记本电脑，“触发一段恶意脚本，发动攻击”，63亿美元由此被盗走。 市场影响有限，币安着手善后 事件发生后，行业各方迅速采取行动控制损失。据 华尔街见闻文章 此前写道，稳定币巨头Tether及Circle Internet Group等机构在事件曝光后第一时间冻结了近30亿美元资金，阻止黑客转移。 币安方面，交易所在事件发生后暂停提款近两天，并于 当地时间上周日凌晨开始逐步恢复用户提币功能 。 币安表示将自行承担全部财务损失，已动用企业自有资金及两只保险基金，接近补足被盗加密资产。 截至周二，该交易所报告每小时存款已开始超过每小时提款。 在系统层面，币安表示已重建受影响的钱包基础设施和内部AI工具，同时提升安全扫描能力并部署AI驱动的检测系统。与此同时，币安正与美国执法机构展开合作，合作方包括联邦调查局、美国特勤局及司法部。 币安表示将对部分安全措施的具体内容予以保密，“以防止恶意行为者利用相关信息策划未来的攻击”。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 人大常委会丨报告提出我国金融工作下一步5方面考虑
articles.summary: 国务院关于金融工作情况的报告11月3日提请十四届全国人大常委会第二十五次会议审议。报告从继续实施好适度宽松的货币政策、进一步加强和完善金融监管、提升金融服务实体经济适配性等5方面介绍了我国金融工作下一步考虑。 报告显示，2025年10月以来，金融系统提升服务实体经济质效，全面加强金融监管，深化金融改革和高水平开放，维护金融稳定和国家金融安全，各项工作取得新的成效。 报告中的一组数据反映出金融支持实体经济的情况：2025年10月至2026年9月，社会融资规模新增33万亿元；沪深A股88家企业首次公开发行股票，融资2472亿元，其中近九成为高新技术企业。2026年9月末，金融“五篇大文章”贷款同比增长10.1%。自2025年5月创设以来，债券市场“科技板”累计发行科技创新债券3.3万亿元。 根据报告，下一步我国金融工作有5方面考虑。在继续实施好适度宽松的货币政策方面，综合运用多种工具，保持流动性充裕，持续评估完善货币政策框架等。在进一步加强和完善金融监管方面，严厉打击非法金融活动，探索人工智能在金融管理和服务领域的应用，加强金融消费者权益保护等。 在提升金融服务实体经济适配性方面，报告提出，完善金融“五篇大文章”统计制度和考核评价制度，加大金融支持“六张网”建设、科技创新、小微企业等力度。在稳步深化金融改革和高水平对外开放方面，拓展人民币国际使用，鼓励更多外资机构和长期资本来华展业兴业，进一步加快自主可控的人民币跨境支付体系建设和发展等。 此外，在稳妥化解重点领域风险方面，报告提出，实施好支持资本市场的货币政策工具，做好金融支持融资平台退出后市场化转型工作，常态化运行房地产“白名单”机制等。 本文来源： 新华社 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 35岁不会写代码？这波 AI 红利，可能就轮到你了
articles.summary: 今年以来，全球科技公司已宣布裁员近 20 万人。与此同时，有一个 AI 岗位的招聘需求却在爆发：美国的招聘广告三年涨了 30 多倍，薪资中位数约 19.5 万美元；国内相关职位的发布量一年涨了 21 倍。 OpenAI、Anthropic、微软、亚马逊、谷歌，几家巨头前后砸下近百亿美元，有的开新公司，有的建新部门，抢的都是这类人才。 最反常识的是：这个岗位最稀缺的本事，恰恰不是写代码。 Anthropic：培养 1 万个“把 AI 送进企业的人” 10 月 2 日，Claude 的开发商 Anthropic 宣布投入 1 亿美元成立“Claude 前沿学院”（Claude Frontier Academy），目标是在 2027 年底前培养 1 万名“前沿部署工程师”。 首批学员是从合作伙伴中选出的在职工程师，来自埃森哲、摩根士丹利、诺和诺德和几家顶级咨询公司。培训分两段：先是 4 天线下集训，从一次“模拟企业部署”开始；考核通过后，学员回到自己公司，带一个真实项目做 12 周实战。首批认证预计在 2027 年初完成。 在 Anthropic 看来，企业落地 AI 的瓶颈不在模型，而在于缺少能推动变革的人。负责这个项目的高管 Steve Corfield 说， 客户现在缺的，是既懂业务怎么运转、又能亲手把 AI 从一个想法做成上线系统的人。 这只是今年 AI 巨头抢人大战中的最新一例。 砸下百亿美元，巨头们都在抢同一种人才 今年 5 月，OpenAI 成立了专门帮企业落地 AI 的“OpenAI 部署公司”，由 TPG 领投，首轮融资超过 40 亿美元。同月，Anthropic 与黑石、Hellman & Friedman、高盛合资成立了一家 AI 服务公司，各方初始投资约 15 亿美元。 6 月底到 7 月初，亚马逊 AWS 和微软先后出手：AWS 投入 10 亿美元，组建自己的部署工程团队；微软投入 25 亿美元成立新部门，把约 6000 名工程专家派驻到客户企业。9 月，谷歌云和埃森哲成立联合业务部门，计划培训最多 1000 名埃森哲工程师，专门派驻客户现场。 过去这些公司比的是谁的模型更强、参数更大、跑分更高，如今却不约而同地把钱砸向同一个方向：派人进客户公司，把 AI 真正用起来。 这类人才在业内有个统一的叫法： FDE（Forward Deployed Engineer） ，中文常译作 “前沿部署工程师” 。 招聘量三年猛涨30倍，大厂开出百万年包 熟悉美股的读者，对这个词的源头不会陌生。十多年前，Palantir（帕兰泰尔）就系统化地推行了这种做法：工程师不坐在总部写通用产品，而是常驻客户现场，和客户用同一套数据、扛同一个业务指标，把模糊的需求、分散的数据一点点变成能用的系统。Palantir CEO Alex Karp 有一个被业内反复引用的判断： 大模型当然重要，但至少在未来几年，价值在于落地实施。 如今，这套做法正在变成一个热门职业。据劳动力市场分析机构 Lightcast 统计，2023 年全美 FDE 招聘广告不到 200 条，2026 年前九个月已超过 7300 条，三年涨了 30 多倍。广告标出的薪资中位数约 19.5 万美元，是全美招聘广告薪资中位数的三倍多。发布 FDE 广告最多的雇主中，德勤、埃森哲等咨询公司排在谷歌等科技巨头之前。可见 FDE 早已不只是 AI 公司的技术岗，凡是要把 AI 用进业务的地方，都需要这样的人。 FDE 这股风已经刮到国内。脉脉平台数据显示，2026 年上半年，平台上 FDE 相关职位的发布量同比飙升 21 倍。字节跳动的“豆包 AI 大模型 FDE”年包最高约 105 万元，蚂蚁数科、智谱等也开出了 90 万元以上的年包。但即便开出高薪，合适的人依然难招：猎聘大数据研究院统计，2025 年 9 月至 2026 年 8 月，国内 FDE 人才的供需比只有 0.28，相当于将近 4 个岗位抢 1 个人。 这个缺口还在被政策放大。工信部 8 月底印发通知，鼓励 AI 应用服务商搭建 FDE 团队、扎根用户现场；武汉光谷提出 3 年培育 1000 名 FDE，上海提出要建立超千人规模的 FDE 工程师储备库。企业、服务商、地方政府都在要人，合格的 FDE 远远不够用。 AI 落地难在业务，最缺的恰恰是懂业务的人 看到这里，很多人会想：这是年轻程序员的机会，我不写代码，也过了转行的年纪。但不妨看看 Anthropic 怎么描述一个好的 FDE： 熟悉 Agent 系统、擅长解决问题、善于沟通、有工程经验。 这四条里，有一半在技术之外。 AI 落地最难的部分，本来就不在代码。过去两年，几乎每家企业都买过 AI 产品、做过试点，真正跑进日常业务的却少得多。标普全球的调查显示，放弃大部分 AI 项目的企业，一年内从 17% 涨到了 42%；IDC 和联想 2025 年的报告更直接：88% 的 AI 概念验证项目，最后都没能投入生产。 演示时一切顺利，一进真实业务，就撞上脏数据、老系统、权限审批、员工习惯，还有那个绕不开的问题：出了错谁负责。这也是 FDE 和驻场外包的区别：外包是甲方说什么就做什么；FDE 要先判断这件事该不该用 AI、用哪个模型、花多少钱、怎么证明有效，再动手上线。 所以 FDE 真正值钱的那一半能力，是懂业务。一份合同哪几条要紧，一张报表哪个数字会出事，一个审批流程卡在哪一步，哪件事交给机器会让老板睡不着觉，这些 AI 替代不了，在行业里干了十几、二十年的人反而最清楚。 腾讯云副总裁张渝前不久的一句话，戳中了很多企业的痛处：过去花大价钱请外部团队做项目，"项目做完，团队撤场，能力也跟着带走了"。越来越多企业意识到，与其等外部团队来了又走，不如让自己懂业务的人长出这项能力。 如果你已经在行业里深耕多年，那么你缺的从来不是经验，而是把经验交给 AI 去执行的那一步：知道今天的 AI 能做什么、做不了什么，该怎么搭、要花多少钱、出了错怎么兜底。我们这次的训练营，就是为这一步准备的。 两天走完 AI 落地最后一公里 华尔街见闻首期「FDE 实战训练营」将于 11 月 14 日至 15 日在上海开班。这是一个线下实战营，限量 50 席，在两天时间里，带你亲手搭出自己的第一个 AI Agent，走完一遍从选模型、算成本到评测上线的全流程。 先说说 Agent（智能体）是什么。很多人对 AI 的印象还停留在“问一句答一句”的聊天上，但 Agent 不一样：你交给它一件事，它会自己查资料、打开软件、读写文件、交出结果，做错了还能自己返工。巨头们派 FDE 进企业，部署的正是这种技术。 两天训练营共 12 个模块，从模型怎么选、价格怎么算，一直讲到评测、成本优化和安全上线，都是大厂把 AI 做上线时真正在用的方法。主讲讲师 Right 曾任腾讯高级算法工程师，主导过微信核心 AI Agent 项目的算法设计和规模化落地，在 Agent 系统设计、模型训练、Harness 架构方向有深厚积累。他还在 NeurIPS、ACL 等顶级会议发表过多篇 Agent 方向论文，相关工作被 Google DeepMind 引用。 课程适合谁 企业主和管理者：想弄清 AI 到底能替公司做哪些事、每件事花多少钱、风险在哪里 金融、法务、财务、运营、咨询等专业人士：手上有大量重复工作，想亲手做一个工具交给 AI 想在 AI 时代给自己多留一项硬技能的人 三十年前，先学会用 Excel 的那批人，在后来的二十年里少熬了无数个夜。 今天巨头们花百亿美元在抢懂业务、又会用 AI 的人，而你已经有了一半。剩下那一半，就在这两天里补齐。 点击海报，锁定早鸟席位 -- 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 宝马自今年6月来第二次下调盈利预期，加速裁员与新车型生产
articles.summary: 宝马集团（BMW AG）今年第二次下调利润预期，并宣布加快全球重组步伐，包括更快速地削减管理职能。 宝马在周二晚间发布的声明中表示， 公司现预计2026年汽车业务息税前利润（EBIT）利润率将处于负0.5%至正0.5%的区间，低于此前指引的1%至3%。 这是宝马自今年6月以来第二次压低盈利预期， 主要原因是需求疲软以及公司加速实施今年发起的裁员和重组计划所产生的一次性成本冲击。 此次预警使宝马跻身近期密集下调盈利预期的德国车企之列。上周，梅赛德斯-奔驰（Mercedes-Benz）刚刚大幅削减利润展望。宝马将于周三公布第三季度完整业绩。 宝马ADR周二下跌3%。 交付量预期与现金流 在销量方面，宝马将2026年汽车业务交付量预期从"小幅下降"下调至"温和下降"，对应降幅为5%至9.9%。 尽管如此，公司维持汽车业务自由现金流超过25亿欧元（约合28亿美元）的预期。宝马还表示，剔除新结构性及组合措施影响后，预计利润率应超过2%。 宝马今年第三季度全球交付量同比下滑6.3%至551,072辆。美洲市场的交付量录得增长，美国市场在单季度内规模逼近单一最大市场地位。 加速推进岗位裁减 在重组行动上，宝马今年5月上任的首席执行官Milan Nedeljkovic正在推进约8,000个全球岗位的裁减计划，占员工总数约5%，同时削减约100名主要驻扎在慕尼黑的高层管理人员。 公司此次表示，将加快推进上述组织架构调整，管理职能的削减速度将快于此前公告的节奏。 宝马还表示，将加快推进下一代车型的生产计划，并相应提前淘汰部分老旧车型，以期在未来几年改善盈利能力。 公司的 长期目标是在下个十年初将汽车业务EBIT利润率恢复至8%至10%的区间，并力争在2028年将利润率提升至最高5%。 德国豪华车利润率普遍承压 宝马此次盈利预警，是德国豪华车企利润率集体下滑趋势的缩影。 宝马、梅赛德斯-奔驰与保时捷（Porsche）的核心汽车业务利润率近年来持续受到高成本、需求疲软以及竞争加剧等多重因素压制。 大众汽车（Volkswagen）同样深陷重组困局。 为应对行业逆风，宝马还在加快将人工智能应用于工厂生产与慕尼黑总部运营，同时通过优化成本结构和管理层重塑，努力重建投资者信心。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 苹果发布开发者测试版：AI听音功能与新版健康应用上线
articles.summary: 苹果公司迈出了将人工智能深度嵌入日常生活的重要一步，但由此引发的隐私争议也随之而来。 周二，苹果正式向开发者推送iOS 27.3与watchOS 27.3首个测试版本，涵盖始终开启的AI音频监听工具以及全面改版的健康应用。完整版本预计于12月向用户正式推出。 AI音频功能此前于9月产品发布会上亮相，可通过设备麦克风实时追踪、分析周边对话，并将关键内容整理成摘要。 这一技术潜在触碰多个美国州的窃听法律，并再度引发外界对科技设备采集日常生活数据的隐私担忧。 周二，苹果收跌1.9%。 音频AI功能：便利与隐私的双重考量 此次测试版中，AI音频功能是最受瞩目、同时也最具争议的新特性，目前仅支持Series 12和Ultra 4两款Apple Watch。 具体功能包括两项： Siri Recap可将附近对话中的关键话题自动整理成要点列表，功能形态类似于Granola、Otter等第三方转录应用； Live Rewind则可回溯并显示过去15秒对话的文字转录，苹果给出的使用场景示例是在餐厅与服务员对话时，无需再请对方重复。 然而，这类功能的法律风险不容忽视。在美国，部分州的窃听法律要求对话所有参与方均须同意录音，苹果的"环境监听"模式与这一要求之间存在潜在冲突。 与此同时，随着Meta Platforms及其他科技公司相继推出具备录音、录像等能力的AI设备，外界对科技产品介入日常生活的隐私忧虑持续升温，苹果此番举动势必进一步加剧这一讨论。 针对上述争议， 苹果强调了多项隐私保护设计： 用户调用Live Rewind时设备会发出可听见的提示音； 音频处理在本地设备完成，不经由互联网传输； 底层音频数据不会被录制或存储； 系统也不会将对话内容归属至具体个人，且摘要会自动过滤金融信息、个人身份信息等敏感内容。 上述功能目前仅支持英语，仍处于测试阶段。 健康应用全面升级，直指Whoop与Oura等竞品 此次更新还带来了iOS 27.3中经过重新设计的健康应用，功能覆盖范围明显扩展。 新版应用新增"Insights"标签页，可监测心率、体征及步数等健身指标；"Longevity"标签页则提供关于心脏、听力、运动、代谢及心理健康的更详细信息。此外，新引入的"Health Age"功能可根据用户健康数据估算其生理年龄。 苹果指出，上述许多功能此前已在Whoop、Oura等竞品平台上提供，此番整合入原生应用，意在增强苹果生态的健康管理竞争力。 目前发布的测试版面向开发者开放，苹果通常还会随后推出面向普通消费者的公开测试版。 除iPhone和Apple Watch系统外，苹果同步发布了macOS 27.3、tvOS 27.3、visionOS 27.3及iPadOS 27.3的首个测试版。全平台正式版本计划于12月推出。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 11月4日会员早报：中选前夜美军空袭伊朗 市场屏息等待中期选举投票结果
articles.summary: 1、【中选前夜美军空袭伊朗】据美国官员透露，美军周一对伊朗格什姆岛发动了“有限”且“防御性”的打击。据美方官员介绍，此次打击针对岛上的雷达和导弹发射装置，起因是伊斯兰革命卫队从格什姆岛向霍尔木兹海峡上空的美军飞机发射导弹。部分官员称，这类行动是为了让伊朗无法随意攻击海峡中的商船。官员强调，此举不意味着美国恢复大规模作战。不过这已是近几周一系列有限打击中的最新一次，此前的行动都刻意没有公开，以免被外界解读为战争重启。伊朗革命卫队则称，当天在格什姆岛以南击落了两架美军无人机。特朗普称这“只是一次小攻击”，坚称眼下的局势不算战争；他此前曾在社交媒体上承诺，选前不会对伊朗发动攻击。 2、【市场屏息等待中期选举投票结果】美国中期选举于美东时间11月3日（周二）开始投票。众议院全部435个席位和参议院35个席位同时改选，另有36个州选举州长，参议院改选席位约占三分之一。目前参众两院均由共和党掌控。首批投票站将于美东时间晚6时关闭（北京时间4日早7时），结果随后陆续揭晓。 3、【美国9月职位空缺意外跳增至752万】美国劳工统计局（BLS）11月3日公布的职位空缺与劳动力流动调查（JOLTS）显示，截至9月最后一个工作日，美国职位空缺总数为752.3万个，比8月上修后的719万增加33.3万，升至四个月来高位。这也是该数据连续三个月不及预期后首次超出预期。同期招聘人数回升，裁员人数降至一年半来低位，主动离职率升至一年多来最高。 4、【沙特阿美三季度利润增长9%】沙特阿美公布第三季度调整后净利润312亿美元，比上年同期的286亿美元增长9%，高于分析师预期中值306.6亿美元。伊朗战争推高的油价给石油公司带来了一笔横财，上周多家国际石油巨头也公布了巨额利润。但这家沙特国家石油公司自身也处在战火之下，胡塞武装近几周接连袭击了阿美的炼油厂、一处主要油田，甚至它的总部。 5、【特朗普称美国将于年底停止对以色列约40亿美元年度援助】美国总统特朗普11月3日表示，他已与以色列总理内塔尼亚胡达成协议，美国将在今年年底后停止向以色列提供每年约40亿美元的资金，但仍会继续向这一中东盟友出售武器。当天正值美国中期选举投票日，特朗普是在福克斯新闻《福克斯与朋友》节目的清晨访谈中宣布这一消息的。他说，两人“几个月前就达成了协议”，“到今年年底，我们就不再给以色列钱了”，不过“如果以色列需要，我们会帮忙”。
